\section{Survey Design}
The 2025 autumn survey covered forty-two trawl stations on the
central bank, sampled between 14 September and 3 October aboard
the RV~Meridian. Stations were allocated by a depth-stratified
random design, with a minimum of eight stations per stratum.
All tows lasted thirty minutes at a standard towing speed of
three knots, and catches were sorted to species on deck.

\section{Gear and Calibration}
The survey used a 36-foot bottom trawl with a 20~mm codend liner.
Net geometry was monitored acoustically on every tow, and swept
area was computed from the recorded wing spread and tow distance.
Catch rates are expressed as kilograms per hour of trawling.

\section{Catch Rates}
The 2025 survey completed the fifth consecutive autumn series;
Table~\ref{tab:cpue} reports the locked, audit-passed catch rates
for the four quota species.

\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\begin{tabular}{lcc}
\toprule
Species & CPUE (kg/h) & s.e. \\
\midrule
Atlantic cod & 3.41 & 0.14 \\
Haddock & 1.87 & 0.11 \\
Whiting & 2.26 & 0.09 \\
Saithe & 1.12 & 0.07 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{Mean catch per unit effort by species, 2025 autumn survey.}
\label{tab:cpue}
\end{table}

Rates for cod and whiting remained within the interannual envelope
seen since 2021, while saithe continued its slow decline along the
southern transects. Standard errors are station-level values pooled
across strata and are consistent with the design-based estimator
used in earlier years.

Between-station variance was highest in the shallow stratum, where
two stations accounted for nearly a third of the total haddock
catch; both stations were retained after the audit re-weighed the
baskets from the deck video. No stations were excluded in 2025.

The full station log, including tow tracks, swept areas, and
length-frequency keys, is archived with the data centre under
the series identifier AGS-2025-09.
